Mark Thompson was born on July 13, 1972, in Vancouver, Canada. He grew up in a loving family with parents who instilled in him the importance of education and environmental responsibility.

Thompson attended the Vancouver Technical School, where he excelled in science and mathematics. His interest in environmental conservation led him to pursue a degree in Environmental Science at the University of British Columbia. During his time at university, he became an active member of the student body, participating in various eco-activism groups and volunteering for local wildlife conservation projects.

After graduating from the University of British Columbia with honors, Thompson landed a job as a senior consultant at AECOM, a leading environmental consulting firm. He quickly made a name for himself within the company, known for his expertise in sustainable development and community engagement. Over the years, he collaborated on numerous high-profile projects, including the redevelopment of Vancouver's waterfront area.

Thompson's personal life is marked by a strong sense of independence and self-reliance. Despite having an extensive social network, he has difficulty forming intimate relationships. His closest friends are scattered across the country, and he prefers to maintain a low profile in his personal life. This aloofness stems from unresolved childhood fears of abandonment, which have led him to prioritize his emotional safety over genuine connections with others.

In 2005, Thompson met Emma, a fellow environmentalist who shared his passion for conservation. They started dating casually but never formalized their relationship. Emma eventually moved away to pursue a career opportunity, leaving Thompson feeling relieved and yet unfulfilled.

Throughout his life, Thompson has maintained a modest lifestyle, residing in a small apartment on Robson Street in Vancouver's downtown area. He enjoys spending time alone, exploring the city's hidden gems, and engaging in solo activities like hiking and reading.

In 2010, Thompson received the Environmental Excellence Award from the City of Vancouver for his outstanding contributions to sustainable development and community engagement. This recognition further solidified his reputation as a leading expert in his field, but it also brought him more attention and pressure to perform.

Today, Mark Thompson continues to work at AECOM, where he is respected by his peers for his expertise and dedication. Despite the success and accolades, he remains introspective and guarded, forever struggling with the fear of abandonment and rejection that has defined his life since childhood.
